frases.texto: Don Quixote of La Mancha. Part 4: The Enchanted Cage and Sancho’s Island
frases.fala: Don Quixote of La Mancha. Part 4: The Enchanted Cage and Sancho’s Island

frases.texto: It’s time for the last part of our great journey!
frases.fala: It’s time for the last part of our great journey!

frases.texto: Don Quixote will go back to his village inside a wooden CAGE, set off again in search of adventures, fly through the sky on a wooden horse and see his loyal squire’s dream come true: to rule an ISLAND!
frases.fala: Don Quixote will go back to his village inside a wooden cage, set off again in search of adventures, fly through the sky on a wooden horse and see his loyal squire’s dream come true: to rule an island!

frases.texto: In this goodbye, Sancho Panza will teach all of us that true WISDOM doesn’t come from crowns or riches: it grows in the hearts of simple, generous people.
frases.fala: In this goodbye, Sancho Panza will teach all of us that true wisdom doesn’t come from crowns or riches: it grows in the hearts of simple, generous people.

frases.texto: Turn the page, feel the wind on your face and come and see the ending of this story that the whole world loves!
frases.fala: Turn the page, feel the wind on your face and come and see the ending of this story that the whole world loves!

frases.texto: Chapter 23. The Enchanted Cage. A Journey by Ox Cart
frases.fala: Chapter 23. The Enchanted Cage. A Journey by Ox Cart

frases.texto: To take Don Quixote back home without hurting his feelings, his friends built a big wooden CAGE on top of a cart pulled by two white OXEN, gentle and very slow.
frases.fala: To take Don Quixote back home without hurting his feelings, his friends built a big wooden cage on top of a cart pulled by two white oxen, gentle and very slow.

frases.texto: While the knight was asleep, tired from so many battles, they put him inside very carefully.
frases.fala: While the knight was asleep, tired from so many battles, they put him inside very carefully.

frases.texto: When he woke up behind the wooden bars, Don Quixote didn’t get cross.
frases.fala: When he woke up behind the wooden bars, Don Quixote didn’t get cross.

frases.texto: He smiled, very calm: “I am ENCHANTED by a powerful wizard!” he told his friends.
frases.fala: He smiled, very calm: I am enchanted by a powerful wizard! he told his friends.

frases.texto: “Only the most famous knights in history travel in magic carriages like this one!”
frases.fala: Only the most famous knights in history travel in magic carriages like this one!

frases.texto: And so the cart rolled slowly on across the golden fields: the wheels creaking, the oxen mooing softly, Sancho beside them on his faithful donkey, and Don Quixote waving happily from inside, dreaming of the adventures still to come!
frases.fala: And so the cart rolled slowly on across the golden fields: the wheels creaking, the oxen mooing softly, Sancho beside them on his faithful donkey, and Don Quixote waving happily from inside, dreaming of the adventures still to come!

frases.texto: Chapter 24. Back Home. Hugs in La Mancha
frases.fala: Chapter 24. Back Home. Hugs in La Mancha

frases.texto: At midday on a sunny Sunday, the ox cart arrived in the little village square, and all the neighbours came running to see the travellers.
frases.fala: At midday on a sunny Sunday, the ox cart arrived in the little village square, and all the neighbours came running to see the travellers.

frases.texto: His loving NIECE Antonia and the housekeeper, who looked after the house, gave Don Quixote lots of kisses and happy tears.
frases.fala: His loving niece Antonia and the housekeeper, who looked after the house, gave Don Quixote lots of kisses and happy tears.

frases.texto: They tucked their uncle into a soft bed and gave him some nice hot chicken soup.
frases.fala: They tucked their uncle into a soft bed and gave him some nice hot chicken soup.

frases.texto: Sancho ran to his little white cottage.
frases.fala: Sancho ran to his little white cottage.

frases.texto: His wife, Teresa Panza, and his little daughter, Sanchica, came running to hug him.
frases.fala: His wife, Teresa Panza, and his little daughter, Sanchica, came running to hug him.

frases.texto: “Did you bring gold coins?” asked Teresa.
frases.fala: Did you bring gold coins? asked Teresa.

frases.texto: “Did you bring pretty dresses?” asked Sanchica, jumping for joy.
frases.fala: Did you bring pretty dresses? asked Sanchica, jumping for joy.

frases.texto: “I brought something much more precious!” answered Sancho, swinging his daughter round in the air.
frases.fala: I brought something much more precious! answered Sancho, swinging his daughter round in the air.

frases.texto: “I brought memories I’ll never forget, lots of courage, and I know for sure that one day I’ll rule a lovely island!”
frases.fala: I brought memories I’ll never forget, lots of courage, and I know for sure that one day I’ll rule a lovely island!

frases.texto: Around the table, with homemade bread and olives, the FAMILY listened to the stories of the windmills and the sheep until late at night.
frases.fala: Around the table, with homemade bread and olives, the family listened to the stories of the windmills and the sheep until late at night.

frases.texto: But, looking at the moon through his bedroom window, Don Quixote was already full of LONGING for the magic dust of the open road...
frases.fala: But, looking at the moon through his bedroom window, Don Quixote was already full of longing for the magic dust of the open road...

frases.texto: Chapter 25. Clavileño, the Flying Horse. A Journey through the Sky without Leaving the Ground
frases.fala: Chapter 25. Clavileño, the Flying Horse. A Journey through the Sky without Leaving the Ground

frases.texto: Months later, missing their adventures, the two friends set off again along the roads of the world!
frases.fala: Months later, missing their adventures, the two friends set off again along the roads of the world!

frases.texto: And they had a surprise: their adventures had been written down in a book, and the Knight of the Sorrowful Face was famous all over Spain!
frases.fala: And they had a surprise: their adventures had been written down in a book, and the Knight of the Sorrowful Face was famous all over Spain!

frases.texto: A very rich duke and duchess, who loved that book, invited the two friends to their palace.
frases.fala: A very rich duke and duchess, who loved that book, invited the two friends to their palace.

frases.texto: There, they made up a pretend game: they brought out CLAVILEÑO, a huge wooden horse with a peg in its neck which, they said, made the horse fly above the clouds.
frases.fala: There, they made up a pretend game: they brought out clavileño, a huge wooden horse with a peg in its neck which, they said, made the horse fly above the clouds.

frases.texto: Don Quixote and Sancho climbed onto the horse and covered their eyes with a black BLINDFOLD.
frases.fala: Don Quixote and Sancho climbed onto the horse and covered their eyes with a black blindfold.

frases.texto: To make it feel like flying, the palace servants blew wind at them with big BELLOWS, the kind a blacksmith uses to blow air, and came up close with a hot torch.
frases.fala: To make it feel like flying, the palace servants blew wind at them with big bellows, the kind a blacksmith uses to blow air, and came up close with a hot torch.

frases.texto: “We’re going through the highest clouds!” shouted Sancho, scared and amazed at the same time, holding on tight to his master’s waist.
frases.fala: We’re going through the highest clouds! shouted Sancho, scared and amazed at the same time, holding on tight to his master’s waist.

frases.texto: “And now we’re right next to the sun!”
frases.fala: And now we’re right next to the sun!

frases.texto: “Be brave, Sancho!
frases.fala: Be brave, Sancho!

frases.texto: Hold on tight!” answered Don Quixote.
frases.fala: Hold on tight! answered Don Quixote.

frases.texto: Help the friends on their amazing journey through the sky!
frases.fala: Help the friends on their amazing journey through the sky!

frases.texto: Chapter 26. Advice for a Governor. Sancho Will Rule an Island
frases.fala: Chapter 26. Advice for a Governor. Sancho Will Rule an Island

frases.texto: Carrying on with the game, the duke made Sancho governor of the Isle of Barataria, which was really a pretty town in the countryside, with no sea around it at all!
frases.fala: Carrying on with the game, the duke made Sancho governor of the Isle of Barataria, which was really a pretty town in the countryside, with no sea around it at all!

frases.texto: The evening before he left, Don Quixote sat with his faithful squire on a stone bench in the garden and gave him the wisest ADVICE a friend can give:
frases.fala: The evening before he left, Don Quixote sat with his faithful squire on a stone bench in the garden and gave him the wisest advice a friend can give:

frases.texto: “Sancho, my friend of the road, never be ashamed of being the son of farmers, simple and honest people.
frases.fala: Sancho, my friend of the road, never be ashamed of being the son of farmers, simple and honest people.

frases.texto: Be just as kind to someone with bare feet as to someone who is rich.
frases.fala: Be just as kind to someone with bare feet as to someone who is rich.

frases.texto: Always keep your HUMILITY, look for the truth with patience, and remember: the most beautiful JUSTICE is the kind that walks hand in hand with forgiveness.”
frases.fala: Always keep your humility, look for the truth with patience, and remember: the most beautiful justice is the kind that walks hand in hand with forgiveness.

frases.texto: Sancho listened to every piece of advice with tears in his eyes.
frases.fala: Sancho listened to every piece of advice with tears in his eyes.

frases.texto: He hugged his dear friend, promised to keep every word in his heart and set off to rule the island, very proud, riding on his donkey.
frases.fala: He hugged his dear friend, promised to keep every word in his heart and set off to rule the island, very proud, riding on his donkey.

frases.texto: Chapter 27. The Mystery of the Walking Stick. The Cleverest Judgement
frases.fala: Chapter 27. The Mystery of the Walking Stick. The Cleverest Judgement

frases.texto: On his very first day as the island’s judge, Sancho was given a mystery to solve: a quarrel between two old neighbours.
frases.fala: On his very first day as the island’s judge, Sancho was given a mystery to solve: a quarrel between two old neighbours.

frases.texto: The first one complained: “I lent him ten gold COINS, and he won’t give them back!”
frases.fala: The first one complained: I lent him ten gold coins, and he won’t give them back!

frases.texto: The second one swore, with his hand on his heart: “I swear I have already put every coin back into his hands!”
frases.fala: The second one swore, with his hand on his heart: I swear I have already put every coin back into his hands!

frases.texto: But, before swearing, the second old man asked his neighbour to hold his wooden WALKING STICK.
frases.fala: But, before swearing, the second old man asked his neighbour to hold his wooden walking stick.

frases.texto: He swore, took his stick back and was about to go home, as calm as anything.
frases.fala: He swore, took his stick back and was about to go home, as calm as anything.

frases.texto: Sancho scratched his beard, suspicious: “Hmm...
frases.fala: Sancho scratched his beard, suspicious: Hmm...

frases.texto: Why would someone ask the other man to hold his stick right when he swears?”
frases.fala: Why would someone ask the other man to hold his stick right when he swears?

frases.texto: “Bring that walking stick here!” ordered the governor, with a clever look.
frases.fala: Bring that walking stick here! ordered the governor, with a clever look.

frases.texto: Break the walking stick and find out the secret!
frases.fala: Break the walking stick and find out the secret!

frases.texto: When the stick broke, out rolled the ten gold coins, which had been hidden inside the hollow wood!
frases.fala: When the stick broke, out rolled the ten gold coins, which had been hidden inside the hollow wood!

frases.texto: While he was swearing, the old man really had left the money in his neighbour’s hands, hidden in the stick!
frases.fala: While he was swearing, the old man really had left the money in his neighbour’s hands, hidden in the stick!

frases.texto: Everybody clapped, amazed at the great WISDOM of Governor Sancho Panza!
frases.fala: Everybody clapped, amazed at the great wisdom of Governor Sancho Panza!

frases.texto: Chapter 28. Sancho Chooses his Donkey. The Freedom of a Simple Man
frases.fala: Chapter 28. Sancho Chooses his Donkey. The Freedom of a Simple Man

frases.texto: Sancho ruled the town for ten days, always very honestly.
frases.fala: Sancho ruled the town for ten days, always very honestly.

frases.texto: But life in the palace was tiring: a very strict doctor wouldn’t let him eat anything tasty, the meetings never ended, and all that fuss about being governor took away his peace.
frases.fala: But life in the palace was tiring: a very strict doctor wouldn’t let him eat anything tasty, the meetings never ended, and all that fuss about being governor took away his peace.

frases.texto: One fine morning, in his simple farmer’s clothes, Sancho went to the stable, gave his DONKEY a loving hug round the neck and whispered: “My faithful FRIEND, when I travelled with you, my days were full of peace and joy.
frases.fala: One fine morning, in his simple farmer’s clothes, Sancho went to the stable, gave his donkey a loving hug round the neck and whispered: My faithful friend, when I travelled with you, my days were full of peace and joy.

frases.texto: I would a thousand times rather have my FREEDOM and a piece of bread with an onion than all the feasts of the people who rule a kingdom!”
frases.fala: I would a thousand times rather have my freedom and a piece of bread with an onion than all the feasts of the people who rule a kingdom!

frases.texto: And so, without taking a single coin from the town’s treasure chest, Sancho said goodbye to the island with his head held high: he left without any riches, but with a heart full of goodness and wisdom.
frases.fala: And so, without taking a single coin from the town’s treasure chest, Sancho said goodbye to the island with his head held high: he left without any riches, but with a heart full of goodness and wisdom.

frases.texto: The townspeople wiped away their tears, full of thanks, as they watched that kind governor ride away to find his peace again.
frases.fala: The townspeople wiped away their tears, full of thanks, as they watched that kind governor ride away to find his peace again.

frases.texto: Chapter 29. The Knight of the White Moon. Adventures Live in Books
frases.fala: Chapter 29. The Knight of the White Moon. Adventures Live in Books

frases.texto: On a beach of golden sand in Barcelona, to the sound of the waves, a mysterious knight came riding up, with a silver moon painted on his shield: the Knight of the WHITE MOON.
frases.fala: On a beach of golden sand in Barcelona, to the sound of the waves, a mysterious knight came riding up, with a silver moon painted on his shield: the Knight of the white moon.

frases.texto: He was really young Sansón Carrasco, a dear neighbour from La Mancha, who only wanted to take Don Quixote home safely.
frases.fala: He was really young Sansón Carrasco, a dear neighbour from La Mancha, who only wanted to take Don Quixote home safely.

frases.texto: In the fight on the sand, Don Quixote lost and, like a knight who always keeps his word, he did what he had promised: he put away his lance and went back to his village.
frases.fala: In the fight on the sand, Don Quixote lost and, like a knight who always keeps his word, he did what he had promised: he put away his lance and went back to his village.

frases.texto: Back in his reading room, Alonso Quixano sat by the warm fire, surrounded by the books he loved so much.
frases.fala: Back in his reading room, Alonso Quixano sat by the warm fire, surrounded by the books he loved so much.

frases.texto: Every afternoon, the village children sat on the rug at Grandad Alonso’s feet to hear the stories of the windmill giants, the sheep armies, the flight of Clavileño and the squire who ruled an island with justice in his heart.
frases.fala: Every afternoon, the village children sat on the rug at Grandad Alonso’s feet to hear the stories of the windmill giants, the sheep armies, the flight of Clavileño and the squire who ruled an island with justice in his heart.

frases.texto: “Once upon a time there was a gentleman of La Mancha who dreamed with his eyes wide open...”
frases.fala: Once upon a time there was a gentleman of La Mancha who dreamed with his eyes wide open...

frases.texto: Grandad would begin, with a cheeky twinkle in his eye.
frases.fala: Grandad would begin, with a cheeky twinkle in his eye.

frases.texto: And that is how Don Quixote’s IMAGINATION never went out: it went to live for ever in the hearts of young READERS all over the world.
frases.fala: And that is how Don Quixote’s imagination never went out: it went to live for ever in the hearts of young readers all over the world.

frases.texto: Because whoever reads and dreams of doing good, just like you, never stops riding along the most beautiful roads there are!
frases.fala: Because whoever reads and dreams of doing good, just like you, never stops riding along the most beautiful roads there are!
